proof.text: The coefficient rings O_B are Noetherian discrete valuation rings by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], and their completion ideals are principal. The small-site convention is already part of the statement. A field is Noetherian, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes X and Y Noetherian; [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] makes them finite dimensional. Since their characteristic is p distinct from ell, ell is invertible. These verify the hypotheses of the completed-adjunction and scalar-comparison inputs, including the scheme hypotheses of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. For the constructible direct-image theorem, use the given k-structure on Y and give X the composite structure X \to Y \to \operatorname{Spec} k; f is then a k-morphism by definition. This new structure on X is finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], clause (1) (Stacks 01T3). The pro-etale sites, coefficient sheaves and constructibility conditions depend on the underlying schemes, so changing this auxiliary structure does not change any object or functor in the item.

proof.text: For B=E,L, [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction] supplies completion as a reflector and the constant-coefficient completed adjunction. Its Hom bijection first precomposes with the completion unit and then applies the ordinary derived inverse-image/direct-image adjunction. Transport by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]; its statement identifies the finite-reduction towers and completion units. The right-functor comparison of [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison] identifies the transported right adjoint with the actual ringed-topos F_B. Thus this is exactly the h_B specified in the item, on all derived-complete inputs. Write eta_B and epsilon_B for its unit and counit, and lambda_B for the completion unit preceding P_B.

Both factors of the Hom bijection in Step 2 are O_B-linear. Precomposition with lambda_B is linear, and its inverse is linear because it is a bijective linear map. For the ordinary factor, the tensor-formula module adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] is linear: the adjunct sends x to the image of 1 tensor x, and the inverse sends s tensor x to s times that image. On a K-injective target these formulas are termwise formulas for chain maps and respect chain homotopies; [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] and [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] make these actual derived Hom sets; [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] applies to constant-coefficient direct image because its left adjoint is exact. Multiplying a chain map by a scalar commutes with both formulas. Restriction along the constant-to-completed ring map preserves these scalar actions, and the equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] therefore transports the same linear bijection. This proves O_B-linearity of h_B and its inverse.

proof.text:
Put A=O_E, B=O_L, t=varpi_E and v=varpi_L. Choose an A-basis e_1,...,e_d of B by [lem-sfb-local-field-integral-basis]. In the DVR B, t=u v^e with u a unit and e>=1 by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]; t has positive valuation since the coefficient absolute values are compatible. The ideals (t^n)B=(v^{en}) are cofinal with the v-powers: a compatible family at en determines its m-component by reducing any term en>=m, independently of that choice. Modulo t^n the basis identifies B/t^nB with (A/t^n)^d. These are inverse maps of constant sheaves, and inverse limits commute with the finite coordinate tuples by their universal property. Thus the actual ring map
R_W tensor_{A_W} B_W \to S_W, r tensor b |\to r b,
is an isomorphism: in the chosen basis it is the inverse-limit coordinate isomorphism R_W^d \to S_W. Multiplication agrees because the basis multiplication constants are in A, and the same constants occur in every quotient. This proves S_W=R_W tensor_{A_W}B_W as A_W-algebras, not just abstract finite freeness. The structural maps send each constant e_i to itself and commute with the quotient projections [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Hence the identification holds on both sides of f, with their specified structure maps. Tensor extension is exact since its restriction is a finite direct sum.

proof.text: Work first over the discrete constant rings O_E and O_L, so ordinary inverse image is exact. Write Q_B for this inverse image and C_W^0 for coefficient tensor. Reassociation gives a^0:C_X^0 Q_E \to Q_L C_Y^0. The projection construction in [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows], with the free coefficient O_L in degree zero, is the adjunct of tensoring the ordinary counit with the identity. The change-of-rings adjunction [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] tests an O_L-map with induced source by precomposition with x \to x tensor 1. In this test, the two orders of taking the ordinary f-adjunct and the coefficient adjunct agree: both are the module-adjunction map of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], sending m tensor s to s times the ordinary counit image of m. For the derived test choose an O_L K-injective target by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Its O_E restriction is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], since the finite-free coefficient extension is exact. [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] therefore transfers the chain-map calculation to derived Hom sets, and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] identifies the two coefficient-restriction/direct-image factorizations. by k tensor(r tensor b) |\to rk tensor b, with inverse k tensor b |\to k tensor(1 tensor b). proof.text: The scalar and completion comparisons respect the actual completion units. Indeed, in the constant model C_W^0 is tensor with the finite free A-module B. In a basis this is a finite biproduct. A finite biproduct of strict quotient towers has the finite biproduct of their derived limits: the diagonal/limit Hom adjunction, or the product universal property on K-injective tower resolutions, gives the canonical map and its inverse. That map sends the strict quotient augmentation to the same augmentation. Reassociation sends x tensor b to x tensor b at every quotient, including the tower transitions. Thus completion of C_X^0 Q_A agrees, with its unit, with Q_B C_Y^0 followed by B-completion. The t- and v-adic towers have the cofinal identification of Step 4; alternatively their local vanishing conditions are identical since inverting t is inverting v. [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] fixes the completion map chi as the strict quotient augmentation with zero shifted-product component, and [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] carries it to the constant completion unit. Consequently the a fixed in the statement, after transport and precomposition with the unit, is exactly a^0 of Step 5; the source and target chi maps cancel by naturality. title: Scalar compatibility of the ordinary completed adjunction
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, the field $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, and finite coefficient fields $E\subset L$ inside $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ and chosen uniformizers [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism between finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Work on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For $B=E,L$ and $W=X,Y$, write $R_{B,W}=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{B,W}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and let $\mathcal D_{B,W}$ be the full category of derived-complete $R_{B,W}$-module complexes [def-weil-derived-complete, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $P_B=Lf^*_{\mathrm{comp},B}$ as in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], and let $F_B=Rf_{*,R_B}$ be ordinary ringed-topos derived direct image. Let
$$h_B:\operatorname{Hom}(P_BM,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(M,F_BK)$$
be the canonical completed adjunction bijection: transport the constant-coefficient completion/ordinary-adjunction composite of [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction] through [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], with right-functor identification [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison]. This fixes the bijection independently of any constructible restriction.

For $W=X,Y$, write $C_W(-)=-\otimes^L_{R_{E,W}}R_{L,W}$ for scalar extension. On complete inputs this is the strict-tower integral scalar extension under the canonical comparison of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. Use precisely the canonical comparisons of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension],
$$a:C_XP_E\xrightarrow{\sim}P_LC_Y,\qquad b:C_YF_E\xrightarrow{\sim}F_LC_X.$$
Here the normalization of these canonical comparisons is fixed as follows. Put $V_W=\operatorname{Res}_{R_{E,W}\to R_{L,W}}$, and let $\eta^c_W:1\to V_WC_W$ be the coefficient-adjunction unit $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Let $d:V_YF_L\xrightarrow{\sim}F_EV_X$ be the comparison of the two ringed-topos factorizations [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. The map $b_K$ is the coefficient-adjunction transpose of
$$F_EK\xrightarrow{F_E(\eta^c_{X,K})}F_EV_XC_XK\xrightarrow{d_{C_XK}^{-1}}V_YF_LC_XK.$$
The map $a$ is ordinary pullback/tensor reassociation followed by the unit-compatible completion comparison. All coefficient associators here and in the common-stage construction are the balanced tensor maps $((x\otimes s)\otimes t)\mapsto x\otimes st$, transported by the specified $\chi$ comparisons [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition].
The bijections $h_B$ and their inverses are $\mathcal O_B$-linear. For $M\in\mathcal D_{E,Y}$, $K\in\mathcal D_{E,X}$, $u:P_EM\to K$ and $v:M\to F_EK$, one has
$$h_L\bigl(C_X(u)\circ a_M^{-1}\bigr)=b_K\circ C_Y\bigl(h_E(u)\bigr),$$
$$h_L^{-1}\bigl(b_K\circ C_Y(v)\bigr)=C_X\bigl(h_E^{-1}(v)\bigr)\circ a_M^{-1}.$$
These equalities use the given tensor/completion and ringed-topos comparisons, and respect identity extensions and towers $E\subset L\subset L'$ under their tensor associators. On bounded constructible objects [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], raw scalar localization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] gives the same equalities for the localized bijections and rational scalar extension. Consequently, for the common finite-stage Hom sets of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], taking the $h_B$-adjunct or inverse adjunct of a representative is independent of the common finite coefficient field and of the representative.
